hero.lead: I'm a software engineer with 3+ years building enterprise software, now for U.S. clients at Allata. I work with AI coding agents every day and I'm training in agentic AI and MCP.

workflow.title: How I work with AI
workflow.intro: On client work I build with Claude Code. Around it I set up a few pieces so each session starts with the right context and follows the project's rules.

items.title: Context per project
items.text: Each project has a wiki the agent reads (the LLM Wiki pattern). Sessions start with it and the task board loaded, so I don't explain the codebase again.

items.title: Hooks as guardrails
items.text: The rules that must always hold run as scripts at fixed points of the session, so they don't depend on the model remembering an instruction.

items.title: Skills and plugins
items.text: Tasks I repeat become skills, like reviewing a pull request or closing a work item. I write the steps and checks once and reuse them.

items.title: Tuned over time
items.text: I keep adjusting what gets loaded and when, to get better output with fewer tokens.

workflow.note: So far I've used RAG, LangChain, LangGraph and n8n only in training and personal projects.

items.text: Software engineer on enterprise projects for a U.S. client. I work with their stakeholders every day on estimates, technical decisions and code reviews. I also set up the project's AI coding workflow, built on Claude Code with custom hooks, skills and plugins.
Built full stack features for U.S. enterprise clients inside existing architectures, with AI tools at every step. I raised risks early with the team and the client.
Built backend services with Python/Django, Java/Spring Boot, Kotlin and .NET, and Vue.js frontends, mostly on MongoDB. I also wrote custom Odoo ERP modules and helped with ETL and Power BI reports.

Built enterprise applications with C#/.NET and Angular, and managed PostgreSQL and SQL Server databases. My accounting background and data analysis helped me find and ship improvements in several internal systems.

wallstreetpro.title: WallStreetPro
wallstreetpro.text: A swing trading analysis system that runs on Claude Code. Once a week it reads live chart data from TradingView through an MCP server, checks a short rule set and answers BUY or NO BUY with entry, stop and exit date. It never places an order.
wallstreetpro.text2: I backtested the rules on 5,533 simulated trades (446 tickers, 2015 to 2026). They had no edge over the market, so in version 5 I dropped half of the 10 guardrails and kept the ones the data supported.
wallstreetpro.tableCaption: Pass conditions, written before the run

dockwitcher.title: Dockwitcher
dockwitcher.text: A logistics platform that puts fleet and loading dock management in one place, with real-time tracking and notifications. Built during the Full Stack Bootcamp at Hotaka iKhodi.
dockwitcher.alt: Dockwitcher screen listing warehouse receptions with their status

chocolate.title: Chocolate shop e-commerce
chocolate.text: A freelance online store for a chocolate shop, built in 2023. Customers browse and buy, and members get benefits.
chocolate.more: The owners manage stock, promotions and sales reports. Angular front end, with a Node.js and Express API on MySQL.
chocolate.alt: Home page of the chocolate shop store

pallets.title: Pallet management system
pallets.text: A .NET application for pallet logistics. It tracks pallet movements and condition, the carriers and clients involved, and produces inventory reports.
pallets.alt: Control panel of the pallet management system, with monthly movement charts

pasta.title: Pasta Studio, launch landing page
pasta.text: Landing page I designed and built for the April 2026 opening of Pasta Studio, an Italian restaurant in Córdoba, Argentina. It was made to be opened from a QR code on a phone.
pasta.more: Vite and vanilla JavaScript, no framework. It has a live countdown, scroll-snap navigation and Google Maps. The repo holds my version; the owners have changed the site since.
pasta.alt: Pasta Studio landing page with a countdown to the opening
